sources.title: System Design Primer: Security

sources.title: OWASP: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Context-specific encoding, safe sinks, maintained rich-HTML sanitization and CSP defense in depth.

sources.title: OWASP: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Source-to-sink reasoning and safe text construction, with distinct execution and rendering contexts.

sources.title: OWASP: Session Management Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Opaque session lifecycle, cookie scope, regeneration, expiry and server-side invalidation; flags do not replace authorization/CSRF controls.

sources.title: OWASP: Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
sources.supportRationale: Framework token protection, signed/session-bound double submit, origin and SameSite defense boundaries; CORS is not universal CSRF protection.

scenarios.theme: HTML-escaped input becomes an unsafe link. Why?
scenarios.assumptions: The value is placed into a URL-capable context and its scheme/target is not validated. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) to url context.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: HTML-escaped input becomes an unsafe link. Why?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use supported safe URL construction and an explicit allowed scheme/target policy appropriate to the feature, alongside context-correct attribute rendering.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Restrictions can reject legitimate links

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Encoding text for one context does not determine whether the resulting URL is permitted or executable.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) to dom fragment.

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Server-side input handling cannot fix data the browser interprets independently.

scenarios.theme: A team leaves unsafe HTML in place because CSP is enabled. Is that complete?
scenarios.assumptions: The policy and third-party script behavior may change across deployments. What will you do and why?

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) to csp only.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A team leaves unsafe HTML in place because CSP is enabled. Is that complete?

scenarios.theme: Injected script cannot read HttpOnly cookies but performs transfers. What was missed?
scenarios.assumptions: The script runs in the legitimate origin and can issue authenticated actions. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) to cookie unreadable.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Injected script cannot read HttpOnly cookies but performs transfers. What was missed?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Fix the XSS source/sink, enforce action authorization/assurance, investigate effects and credential/session risk, and retain properly scoped cookie/CSRF co

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Additional protections add friction/operations

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Cookie-read restriction does not remove the browser’s authenticated request capability or make same-origin malicious code harmless.
